gloss: throwaway price; rock-bottom price; dirt-cheap price

definitions.gloss: throwaway price; rock-bottom price; dirt-cheap price
definitions.explanation: A price so low it is as if the item were being thrown away — used for goods sold well below market value, often in clearance sales, distressed sales, or urgent liquidations.

examples.english: To sell at a throwaway price.

examples.japanese: {閉店|へいてん}セールで{捨|す}て{値|ね}になっていた。
examples.english: At the closing sale, prices had dropped to throwaway levels.

examples.japanese: {急|きゅう}に{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}すことになり、{家具|かぐ}を{捨|す}て{値|ね}で{処分|しょぶん}した。
examples.english: Having to move suddenly, I got rid of the furniture at dirt-cheap prices.

notes:
Literally "abandonment price" — a price treated as if the seller is simply discarding the item.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {捨|す}て{値|ね}で{売|う}る: to sell at a throwaway price
- {捨|す}て{値|ね}で{買|か}う: to buy at a rock-bottom price
- {捨|す}て{値|ね}になる: (prices) drop to throwaway levels
- {捨|す}て{値|ね}{処分|しょぶん}: disposal at rock-bottom prices

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {格安|かくやす}: bargain price — implies good value but not necessarily desperate selling
- {叩|たた}き{売|う}り: fire sale — emphasizes aggressive, urgent selling
